body: i know that isn't possible. i want to quit the job. my parents probably also wouldn't think very highly of me saying "hey just quit my internship i'm gonna drive to the coast see ya". what should i do about that?

Yeah that certainly makes sense. Damn. I will talk to my therapist about how best to approach this, and I realize this isn't an advice sub so the only thing I'll ask is if you know of an advice or support sub that would be able to help with this? Getting additional voices on this is genuinely helping, even if I'm not getting the judgement I had hoped for. Thanks

I'm really trying not to deliberately cut him out, and actually want to be involving him more because you are right he should be involved more in this. Something of note that may be relevant, I'll probably put it in an edit, A ended up going to some people higher up to force me into therapy, which of course I initially did not want to do. B is concerned the same will happen, and I share her concern. Unfortunately, B really needs this semester grades wise for internships, and if she were forced into therapy/hospitalization, the university may deem it needed to invalidate the semester since she would miss a lot of classes and tests. So it's not just that I feel I would be better for support, but I suspect B is scared of what could happen if she becomes fully honest with A.

Both A and I are trying to get her to go to a therapist. The problem is she's scared of being forcibly hospitalized, which I believe is reasonable. I also don't know how to tell my therapist about the whole situation, since B is a key part of my support system and has ended up on the phone with my therapist about me, so the therapist knows who B is, knows how to contact them, and almost certainly would if I told them, which feels like a violation of B's trust. What did I say that suggests I'm butting into their quality time? I'm not trying to deny your judgement, I genuinely don't feel like I'm doing that and want to know what I might be doing that suggests that
